subject: Stillwater pilot: hosting option tradeoffs (latency vs throughput) + next steps
content:
From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alex Gomez <alex.gomez@stillwater.health>, procurement@stillwater.health
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 25 Aug 2026 16:15:00 -0700
Subject: Stillwater pilot: hosting option tradeoffs (latency vs throughput) + next steps

Hi Alex / procurement team —

Thanks again for a constructive call today. Short recap and suggested next steps so we’re aligned:

- Recap of needs: Stillwater wants a pilot for the recommendation API with P95 latency <= 75ms at peak QPS ~180 and steady-state QPS ~60.
- Risk profile: low tolerance for tail latency spikes during checkout windows (15–30 minute bursts) and strict data partitioning for PHI-adjacent metadata.

Quick recommendation (high level):
- Start with a short Dedicated-capacity pilot (reserved GPU pool) for the first 4 weeks to validate sustained throughput and latency under production-like burst patterns.
  - Why: continuous batching + reserved capacity keeps tail variance predictable; gives you the fastest path to hitting P95 targets without complex local infra.
- Add Hosted API fallback for non-critical routes and development traffic to lower incremental cost while we stress the Dedicated pool.
- If you need on-prem VPC for regulatory reasons, we can scope an option in parallel — that typically adds ~4–6 weeks and some integration work.

Attachments: I’ve attached a short latency profile template (stillwater_latency_profile.csv) and a draft pilot scope (pilot_scope_v1.pdf) to capture the exact workload shape we discussed.

Next steps (proposal):
1) Alex: confirm whether procurement needs a formal SOW before a pilot kick-off (you mentioned possibility).
2) Stillwater: share any historical QPS traces or representative csv of traffic spikes (fill the latency profile).
3) Redwood: we’ll schedule a follow-up technical sync with our runtime team (Ben) to walk the Dedicated pilot config and fallback routing.

Proposed times for the tech sync: Thu 8/27 10–11am PT or Fri 8/28 1–2pm PT. I’ll hold Thu for now unless you prefer the other slot.

Best,
Irene

Irene / Marissa / Alex —

Quick update ahead of today’s sync: I attached a short bench file (stillwater_latency_profile.csv) with our simulated burst run at 400 QPS for 30 minutes and a sustained 200 QPS baseline. Highlights:
- Median token latency looks good; P95 at 400 QPS (simulated) is ~68ms with the Dedicated config I sketched (4x A100 equiv, optimized kernel selection, prewarmed KV cache).
- Observed tail variance came from transient cache cold warms — we reduce this with a small prewarm window and adaptive prefix caching.
- Next step: I’ll bring the exact Dedicated pool config (instance sizes, batch queue thresholds, routing fallback rules) to the call and share a short slide with expected cost delta vs Hosted.

Attachment: stillwater_latency_profile.csv (CSV stub: columns: timestamp,qps,p95_latency_ms,median_latency_ms)
